label: Troll: huge (2.4-2.8 m), kyphotic, long-armed (hands to the knee), grey-green, square-cube heavy
sources: Square-cube scaling and gait in large animals (duty factor and no aerial phase with size) - https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8214834/

notes.generated: by scripts/derive_species.py from the realistic preset - edit its knobs, not this file
notes.bmi: square-cube: a body scaled up keeps its density, so mass grows as H^3 and BMI as H. A human at BMI 27 scaled to 2.6 m is BMI 40 [measured, scaling law]

knobs.heads: the design's 7 at 2.6 m: a small head for the bulk [folklore]
knobs.leg: legs a little short against the trunk [folklore]
knobs.reach: hands to the knee: hanging fingertips at the knee [folklore]
knobs.neck: the head slung forward on a short neck
knobs.girth: square-cube: bone section grows faster than length for the load [measured, scaling law]

notes.skin: grey-green, stony. Every red-shifted region is off: a troll's hide has no blood showing through; the paler palms, soles and nails stay
notes.ratios: fractions of the final standing stature (spine curve applied), as presets.json; tolerances are the realistic preset's scaled with the value and by 1.3
notes.proportion: not graded: the trunk (neck base - hip joint), upper/lower segment ((H - crotch) / crotch), relative sitting height (~1 - crotch) and hanging reach, with the human's beside
notes.segments: bone length factors against the pre-warp human (pre_warp); girth and widths likewise absolute. The warp solves the final factors so the measured joints land on `ratios`

hip_above_crotch.note: the human range scaled with this species' hip-to-crotch gap

pre_warp.note: H_pre = H * stature_factor (stature: the H_pre range). Outside min/max_stature, fit at the limit and scale every segment, girth and width factor by H_pre / limit (a uniform scale)

spine.note: extra bend over a human's; thoracic forward, lumbar back, spread evenly over each span

moves.notes: large-animal gait from the mass (~300+ kg): straight legs, duty factor up, no aerial phase - a run is a fast walk [measured, animals]. The forward lean while walking is a posture on top of the rest-pose hunch
